name: Sundarbans
fact: The largest mangrove forest in the world and home of the Royal Bengal tiger. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Kuakata Sea Beach
fact: Known as the daughter of the sea, one of the few beaches where you can watch both sunrise and sunset.

name: Cox's Bazar Sea Beach
fact: One of the longest natural sea beaches in the world, about 120 km of unbroken sand.

name: Saint Martin's Island
fact: The only coral island of Bangladesh, in the Bay of Bengal.

name: Inani Beach
fact: A rocky coral beach south of Cox's Bazar.

name: Himchari
fact: Hills and a small waterfall right beside the Cox's Bazar coast.

name: Nijhum Dwip
fact: A remote island in Noakhali, famous for its spotted deer.

name: Patenga Beach
fact: Chattogram's sea beach at the mouth of the Karnaphuli River.

name: Foy's Lake
fact: A man-made lake among the hills of Chattogram, built in 1924.

name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
fact: The only freshwater swamp forest in Bangladesh; you explore it by boat.

name: Jaflong
fact: Stone-filled river beside the Khasi hills on the India border.

name: Bichanakandi
fact: Clear water flowing over stones where three hills meet.

name: Lalakhal
fact: A river with striking blue-green water near Jaintiapur.

name: Tanguar Haor
fact: A huge wetland in Sunamganj and a Ramsar site full of migratory birds.

name: Hakaluki Haor
fact: One of the largest haor wetlands in Asia.

name: Sreemangal Tea Gardens
fact: The tea capital of Bangladesh, surrounded by green tea estates.

name: Lawachara National Park
fact: A rainforest known for hoolock gibbons.

name: Madhabkunda Waterfall
fact: One of the highest waterfalls in Bangladesh, in Moulvibazar.

name: Sajek Valley
fact: A hill valley in Rangamati, famous for its sea of clouds.

name: Rangamati Hanging Bridge
fact: The famous bridge over Kaptai Lake.

name: Kaptai Lake
fact: The largest man-made lake in Bangladesh, created by the Kaptai Dam.

name: Nilgiri
fact: A hilltop resort in Bandarban, often above the clouds.

name: Boga Lake
fact: A natural lake about 1,200 feet up in the Bandarban hills.

name: Keokradong
fact: One of the highest peaks of Bangladesh, a popular trek in Bandarban.

name: Nafakhum Waterfall
fact: A wide waterfall on the Sangu River, deep in the Bandarban hills.

name: Somapura Mahavihara, Paharpur
fact: A great Buddhist monastery from the 8th century. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Mahasthangarh
fact: One of the oldest urban sites in Bangladesh, near Bogura.

name: Kantajew Temple
fact: An 18th century temple in Dinajpur covered in terracotta art.

name: Sixty Dome Mosque
fact: The historic mosque city of Bagerhat. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Lalbagh Fort
fact: An unfinished 17th century Mughal fort in Old Dhaka.

name: Ahsan Manzil
fact: The Pink Palace of the Dhaka Nawabs, on the Buriganga River.

name: Panam City, Sonargaon
fact: A street of old merchant houses in the ancient capital of Sonargaon.

name: National Martyrs' Memorial
fact: The national monument in Savar honouring the heroes of 1971.

name: Padma Bridge
fact: The longest bridge in Bangladesh, opened in 2022.

name: Shalban Vihara, Mainamati
fact: Ruins of a Buddhist monastery near Cumilla.

name: Tentulia
fact: The northern tip of Bangladesh, where you can see Kanchenjunga on clear days.

name: Chalan Beel
fact: One of the largest wetlands of Bangladesh, near my home district.
